reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports hardness increase and wear reduction for V addition in Al0.7CoCrFeNi, but it does not address the CoCrFeNi system, the formation of a vanadium-rich oxide tribolayer, or high-temperature behavior up to 800 °C. Key premises about the mechanism and transferability to the proposed matrix are unsupported.
premises: Vanadium addition to Al0.7CoCrFeNi yields a homogeneous bcc solid solution microstructure.
Vanadium addition increases hardness by 33% in Al0.7CoCrFeNi.
Vanadium addition reduces friction wear by 73% in Al0.7CoCrFeNi.
The cited effects are transferable to a CoCrFeNi matrix without Al.
The wear reduction mechanism involves a lubricious vanadium-rich oxide tribolayer.
